exposure: anterior-posterior diameter of the renal pelvis (APRPD) in 2nd and 3rd trimesters
outcome: cause of PNH (idiopathic, polycystic kidney, vesicoureteral reflux, posterior urethral valve)
spontaneous recovery of PNH by six months
cohort: Fetuses diagnosed with prenatal hydronephrosis (PNH) based on specific anterior-posterior diameter of the renal pelvis (APRPD) criteria (>= 4 mm in 2nd trimester and >= 7 mm in 3rd trimester) were included in the study.
finding: The primary finding is that most cases of prenatal hydronephrosis (PNH) are idiopathic, resolve within six months after birth, and moderate to severe PNH in the third trimester is significantly associated with poorer outcomes.
gest_age: fetuses in 2nd and 3rd trimesters of pregnancy; mean gestational age at diagnosis was 20.48 +/- 5.37 weeks
